validated_results.title: Associations of Subtype and Isomeric Plasma Carotenoids with Prostate Cancer Risk in Low-Income African and European Americans.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study evaluating the association between plasma trans-zeaxanthin levels and prostate cancer risk with multivariable-adjusted odds ratios and confidence intervals.

extraction.population: Predominantly low-income African-Americans and European-Americans enrolled in the Southern Community Cohort Study

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 653 controls were included in the study. After exclusion of subjects without race information (n=2) and other ethnicities (n=15), a total of 343 cases and 640 controls (293 cases and 541 controls for African-Americans, and 50 cases and 99 controls for European-Americans) participated in this study.
sample_size.location: METHODS, Case identification and matched controls, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 343 + 640 = 983

cases.excerpt: We conducted a nested case-control study including 343 incident prostate cancer (PCa) cases and 640 controls individually matched on age, race, study site, and time of blood collection.
cases.location: METHODS, Case identification and matched controls, paragraph 1

design.excerpt: We conducted a case-control study nested within the Southern Community Cohort Study (SCCS), a prospective cohort study

timing.excerpt: We conducted a case-control study nested within the Southern Community Cohort Study (SCCS), a prospective cohort study investigating health disparities

continent.excerpt: predominantly low-income African-Americans and European-Americans across 12 Southeastern states.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Plasma concentrations of retinol and carotenoids were determined by high-pressure liquid chromatography (HPLC) with photo diode array detection, as applied previously.
exposure_measurement.location: METHODS, Plasma antioxidant vitamin analysis, paragraph 1
